body:
Tested, works as expected.

The conditions are pretty powerful, I'm a fan. It _does_ let you shoot yourself in the foot by calling functions with side effects, but I'm not opposed to that being a thing that's allowed.

One thing I could see being improved is the text for the "Print" placeholder, I had to resize the window to finish reading it and find out it's with `{var_name}`, it's a minor thing but the text could be condensed or the sizing adjusted.

Checking the validity of the expression within the dialog, if possible, would be great as well, so you can see if you've made a syntax error (I accidentally tried to use `||` instead of `or` for example).

Overall though this is great, very useful and I'd love to see it get merged. Did not look at the code or documentation, just functionality.

I modified the print hint text.

> Checking the validity of the expression within the dialog, if possible, would be great as well, so you can see if you've made a syntax error (I accidentally tried to use `||` instead of `or` for example).

`||` is a valid operator in GDScript.
I added an expression parsing error label but note that it can only catch basic syntax errors.

> The idea of having non-suspending breakpoints is a great one; finally I may no longer have to rely on `print()` statement debugging so much 🙂

Also, no need to search for lost `print()` calls with breakpoints since they all appear in the **Breakpoints** tree! Which reminds me that the tree should show the icons too making it easier to find debug prints. I added it.

> * Using an unknown print name (e.g. `Value of counter: {counters}` instead of `Value of counter: {counter}`) won't replace the placeholder and no error is printed. I'd expect it to print an error (and leave the placeholder as-is).

That's tricky because the user knows what variables to pass for placeholders in a script but the debugger doesn't. It has to pass all the local and member variables as input for the string interpolation so there will always be a `not all arguments converted during string formatting` error if you don't use them all.

As for the other cases, I improved the overall error reporting. They all should link to the source and line now.

> * Since we have some space, we could rename **Suspend Execution** to **Suspend Execution if Condition is Met** just to be clear.

It sounds verbose since there are no other cases the option is relevant. It makes more sense to include a description in the tooltip instead. I added a tooltip for **Enabled** too.

> * When a breakpoint has **Suspend Execution** disabled, it should have a different icon to distinguish it from breakpoints that don't suspend execution. This could be an outlined red circle, for instance. For conditional non-suspending breakpoints, the `=` sign could be present in red in the middle.

I added new icons for non-suspending breakpoints.

> * Changes are occasionally lost after I close and reopen the Edit Breakpoint dialog. It's inconsistent and I can't determine a pattern as to why it's occurring.

I can't reproduce it. I've been using this in my custom build for a while now and never had this issue.

Tested again, works well, great improvements!

I'm not 100% convinced by the icons, in Visual Studio there's a clear difference between what they call a "tracepoint" (a breakpoint that prints and continues executing), which shows up as a diamond shape, and any breakpoint that stops execution which is always a circle, I like this convention just because it's more visible at a glance.

IMO it should be something like:
 * A red circle is an enabled breakpoint that will suspend execution.
 * A red diamond is an enabled breakpoint that won't suspend execution.
 * A red circle with an icon in the middle (plus, minus, equal sign, whichever ends up looking best) is a conditional breakpoint that will suspend execution
 * A red diamond with an icon in the middle is a conditional breakpoint that will not suspend execution

Changing the color to gray or hollowing them out works well for marking them as disabled, and additionally we could have an icon for printing, and another for printing + conditional, but that might be slightly too noisy or hard to read.

An important feature that I believe should be added is a tooltip to the breakpoint that indicates what it does quickly, because right clicking all the way down the big menu to edit the breakpoint just to see what it does is cumbersome when editing code.

This PR vs Visual Studio:
![image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/7c5dc6cb-4fa1-4eb5-a3ed-f0d2a3f5a984)
(Another note is the icon for the conditional breakpoint appears to be blurry and the colors have very little contrast)

Of course, this is just my (very Visual Studio-y) opinion, whichever direction it ends up going this is gonna be a massive help scripting.

JetBrains's "?" is more descriptive. I took the most inspiration from its breakpoint feature for this PR. They use different shapes for different types of breakpoints. A circle for line breakpoints, a bolt for exception breakpoints, and a diamond for function breakpoints. Godot only has line breakpoints so I am not sure if using a diamond even though it's not a different type makes sense. > (Another note is the icon for the conditional breakpoint appears to be blurry and the colors have very little contrast) A problem with the `CodeEdit` implementation is that the textures are white to gray and color-modulated to red so it is hard to have constant with overlayed symbols because everything turns to a single color. The breakpoint colors are exposed to the public API and theme settings so I don't know if I can change this behavior. It should be as simple as setting the default color to white so that modulation has no effect though.
Fixed icon colors in the breakpoint panel and adjusted the gray color.

> Whenever I close and reopen a script, a new breakpoint is added at a line that isn't even in the script:

Fixed.
When editing a breakpoint while the script is closed, it still gets reverted when opening the script. Also, if you restart the editor without opening the script, the edit also isn't saved.

> When editing a breakpoint while the script is closed, it still gets reverted when opening the script. Also, if you restart the editor without opening the script, the edit also isn't saved.

Fixed. I moved the breakpoint editor cache from the script editors to the debugger plugin.
